title: zzop DSL rule pack v1
description: The DSL rule-pack contract (docs/rules/dsl-reference.md; the serde types under crates/core/src/dsl/def/ — the WHOLE directory, never a named subset of it: this sentence used to list two files and a new one silently fell outside every claim made about the mirror). Field names, required-ness, and defaults below mirror the Rust serde types field-for-field: a field is 'required' here exactly when its Rust struct field has neither #[serde(default)] nor an Option type; DSL pack fields are snake_case (packs are DSL-authored data files, not part of the camelCase JS-facing config boundary). Machine-check a pack without a schema validator via the validate_rule_pack MCP tool / `zzop validate-rule-pack <path>` — both run the engine's own loader judgments (structure only, never rule-quality semantics).
$comment: TOLERANCE CONTRACT: additionalProperties is true at every object level — the engine's serde derive silently ignores fields it does not recognize (no deny_unknown_fields anywhere in dsl/def/), same tolerant-input philosophy as the envelope schema (docs/adapters/envelope.schema.json). A pack authored against a FUTURE additive field still loads on an older engine. Only an incompatible revision of the matcher/pack shape itself bumps schema_version (see pack_loader::SUPPORTED_DSL_SCHEMA_VERSION's gate).

id.description: Pack id — the prefix of every finding's ruleId (`<pack id>/<rule id>`) and the unit of same-id collision replacement across packDefs/packsDir layers.

schema_version.description: DSL schema version this pack was authored against. Defaults to 1 when absent; the loader rejects a pack whose version exceeds the engine's SUPPORTED_DSL_SCHEMA_VERSION (currently 1) rather than silently misinterpreting newer fields.

fragments.description: Named regex fragments. A pattern-bearing field below (any field whose description ends '${NAME} fragment reference supported') can be spelled as a whole string EXACTLY `${NAME}` instead of a literal regex — the loader replaces it with the fragment's text before the pack is hashed or evaluated. Merged UNDER a shared bundled fragment set the engine ships (`zzop_core::dsl::fragments`, no filesystem dependency — resolved identically whether the pack arrives from a `packsDir` file or an inline `packDefs` entry): a name declared here WINS a collision against a shared fragment of the same name, letting a pack locally override a shared idiom. `${NAME}` is collision-safe as a sentinel: under the `regex` crate's syntax a bare `{` is only valid as a numeric repetition quantifier, so `${<kebab-case-name>}` can never simultaneously be a value a pack author would hand-write as a real pattern and compile as one. Resolution is single-pass, not recursive — a fragment whose own value is itself a `${...}` reference is a load error, not a silent no-op or a chained expansion. After resolution this map is CLEARED, so a pack authored with fragments and the equivalent pack authored with patterns spelled out inline are load-time indistinguishable (identical cache fingerprint, identical findings). An unresolved/unknown/malformed `${NAME}` reference fails the pack load outright — `zzop validate-rule-pack`/`validate_rule_pack` report it as an issue, same severity as a bad JSON body. Default `{}` for a pack that references only shared fragments, or none at all.

exported_from.description: RETRIEVAL stamp — where this copy of the pack came from. NOT a version of the pack format and NOT a second schema_version: that field says which pack SHAPE the file is written against and gates loading, this one says which zzop BUILD served these bytes and gates nothing. Do not author it by hand. It is minted into the bytes a shipped binary serves for an exported pack (the example-pack-<stem> contract resource) and is absent from every hand-written pack and every copy taken from a source checkout — absence is the normal, silent state, never a defect. When it IS present and its zzop_version differs from the running engine's, each run emits one warnings entry naming both versions and the resource to re-read: a copy retrieved from an older build keeps running that build's rule set, and rules move between packs (and in and out of the bundle) from release to release, so the difference is worth saying even though nothing is skipped and the pack stays fully valid.

rules.description: The pack's rules, evaluated in array order.

packExport.$comment: Deliberately declares no `type`: the referring property (exported_from) owns the object/null choice, and repeating "type": "object" here would make a null value fail this allOf branch. properties/required apply only to object instances, so a null passes vacuously.

zzop_version.description: The zzop version whose binary served these bytes. Compared against the running engine's own version as a plain string — any difference is reported, patch-level included, because a rule moving between packs is an ordinary change rather than a minor-version event.

contract.description: The contract-resource name these bytes were served under (example-pack-<stem>), so the remedy names something that actually resolves. Carried rather than derived from the pack id on purpose: examples/packs/typescript-lint.json declares its id as "typescript", so a name assembled from the id would point at nothing.

id.description: Rule id — combined with the pack id as `<pack id>/<rule id>` in findings. Also the sole source of the rule's inline suppress marker, which is DERIVED as `zzop-<rule id>-ok` (never authored as a field): a `// zzop-<rule id>-ok` comment on the finding's line or the line above suppresses it (`-- zzop-<rule id>-ok` in .sql files; `#` is honored too on the channels whose anchor line can come from any language, so a Python `#` marker works there, AND — per file, on every channel — in every extension whose ONLY comment leader is `#`: .properties/.yaml/.yml/.toml/.ini/.conf/.cfg, `.env` and its `.env.*` siblings, and .py. That roster is not authored here: `HASH_COMMENT_EXTENSIONS` in `crates/core/src/dsl/markers/path.rs` owns it, and this list is a copy that must be re-read against it — .py was added on 2026-08-12 and three shipped sentences went on denying it). Note the marker carries the `zzop-` tool prefix but NO pack prefix — rule `security/hardcoded-secret` suppresses on `// zzop-hardcoded-secret-ok`. Renaming a rule therefore renames its marker too.

axis.description: What KIND of claim this rule makes (zzop_core::dsl::RuleAxis, kebab-case serde form) — the question a reader needs answered before deciding whether a finding is a bug report or a style note. `defect`: wrong regardless of house taste, nobody deliberately ships it (SQL injection, a committed credential, an unauthenticated mutating route). `opinion`: a preference about how code is arranged, where a project that deliberately does the flagged thing is NOT wrong — it disagrees (barrel discipline, `SELECT *`, eager ORM relations). `severity` does NOT stand in for this and was measured not to: it encodes CONFIDENCE x BLAST RADIUS, a different question, so the `info` band holds a real unauthenticated write beside a pure preference and the `warning` band holds opinions. Defaults to `defect` when absent, for two reasons — a pack authored before this field (and every third-party pack) keeps loading unchanged, and a rule that FORGOT to declare should read as the STRONGER claim and be argued down in review rather than quietly demoted to "just an opinion". ⚠ THAT DEFAULT MAKES AN ABSENT FIELD AND A DELIBERATE `"axis": "defect"` INDISTINGUISHABLE ONCE THE PACK IS PARSED — no engine surface can tell them apart, so this field is optional but declaring it is the right call. Packs shipped from this repo may not rely on the default at all: `rule_contracts::rule_axis::every_shipped_rule_declares_its_axis` reads the pack JSON TEXT rather than the loaded rule, because only the text can distinguish a declaration from a silence. A third-party pack has no such test over it, which is exactly why writing the field by hand is worth it — twelve rules that stopped declaring it were described as axis-less by two documents in two days when they were in fact loading as `defect`. Declaring `opinion` carries one obligation: you must be able to name the case in which the flagged shape is the RIGHT call, and the rule's `message` should say so.

scan_test_regions.description: OPT OUT of the test-region gate. By default a finding anchored on a line a parser PROVED is compiled out of the shipping build (`fileProjection.test_spans` in the external-parser contract; `#[cfg(test)]`/`#[test]`-family items for zzop's own Rust frontend) is dropped after the matcher runs, for every matcher kind that reads a file — see docs/rules/dsl-reference.md's 'Test-region exclusion'. Set true and the rule keeps those findings. Set it for exactly one class: a finding about a CREDENTIAL AT REST, where the commit itself is the leak and it makes no difference whether the surrounding code runs — a PEM header or a `scheme://user:pass@host` URL inside a test module is still in git history and still has to be rotated. Every other rule class judges code that RUNS, and test-only code does not run in production, so leave it false. A rule that sets this must NOT also set `file_exclude_pattern`: excluding test PATHS while insisting on test SPANS is the same decision reached both ways at once.

matcher.description: Dispatched on the `type` tag — one of the matcher kinds (zzop_core::dsl::Matcher, kebab-case). line-scan/method-scan read source text (never run in envelope mode); symbol-scan/io-scan query the projected IR (run everywhere); call-scan queries the projected call-site channel, filled by the TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Java, C# and Rust parsers (which FAMILIES each language emits is its producer module doc's contract — Rust, for one, deliberately emits no console-write), so a call-scan rule is silent on the environments with no producer (Prisma, SQL); literal-scan queries the projected bound-string-literal channel, filled by all six structural-parser languages (TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Java, C#, Go, Rust) and empty for Prisma/SQL.

pattern.description: Regex (Rust `regex` crate syntax — no lookaround/backreferences). A non-compiling pattern silently no-ops its rule; `zzop validate-rule-pack` names it. ${NAME} fragment reference supported (used for `any[].pattern`, `patterns[].pattern`, `absent[].pattern`).

label.description: Classification label — lands in the finding's `data.label` (line-scan `any`) or names the pattern for `trigger`/veto roles (method-scan).

type.description: Per-line regex scan over source text. Use either `line_pattern` (single) or `any` (labeled alternatives, first match per line wins).

file_pattern.description: Target file-path regex (e.g. `(?i)\.(java|jsp)$`) — the rule only scans matching files. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

require_file.description: Cheap pre-skip: only scan a file whose whole text matches this regex. Absent = always scan. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

require_file_all.description: Additional pre-skip regexes, ALL of which must match the file text (short-circuits on first miss). Each entry: ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

require_file_absent.description: Negated pre-skip: if ANY of these matches the whole file text, the rule skips the file entirely ("flag X only when there is no Y anywhere in the file"). Each entry: ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

skip_comment_lines.description: Skip lines whose trimmed start opens a comment in THAT FILE's own syntax — `//`, `*`, `/*` for every extension, plus `--` in a `.sql` file (one extension-keyed leader table, not a fixed triple).

strip_string_literals.description: Mask the interior of every closed string literal (single/double-quote and backtick pairs) on a line to spaces before testing `line_pattern`/`any`/`exclude_pattern`, so a token that only appears inside a string literal does not false-fire. The original line still supplies the snippet. Leave false for rules whose intent is to match INSIDE strings (hardcoded-secret, sql-in-string).

line_pattern.description: Regex that flags a line (single pattern, no label). Mutually alternative with `any`. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

any.description: Labeled alternatives — first match per line wins, its label lands in the finding's `data.label`.

exclude_pattern.description: A line matching the main pattern is skipped when it ALSO matches this regex (per-line veto). ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

prev_line_exclude_pattern.description: One-line-lookback veto: a line matching the main pattern is skipped when the IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING line matches this regex. For statement continuations a per-line matcher cannot otherwise see (a formatter-wrapped concise arrow body or assignment) — typically an end-of-line-anchored shape like `(=>|=)\s*$`, not a copy of `exclude_pattern`. Exactly one line, never a window; a rule leaning on it should disclose that in its message. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

line_call_kind.description: Structural gate — a call KIND (a plain string compared for equality, NOT a regex and NOT fragment-expanded). A line that matched `line_pattern`/`any` fires only when the file's projected call sites carry an entry of that kind ON THAT SAME LINE: the regex says the shape is present, this asks the parser whether the line really CALLS the named API family, so the same spelling inside a string literal, a comment, or on an unrelated receiver is not a match. Degrades to SILENCE (call-scan's direction): a file with no projected call sites — a degraded parse, an environment with no producer, or a callee spelling the producer cannot resolve — can never fire a gated rule where the bare regex used to, so a rule setting this must disclose the trade in its own message. Kind spellings: the authoritative list is `zzop_core::RULE_READ_CALL_KINDS` (see callScan.kind — this description defers rather than enumerates, for the same staleness reason).

file_exclude_pattern.description: Path regex — a file whose relative path matches is skipped entirely (the escape hatch for "this extension but NOT under scripts/"). ${NAME} fragment reference supported — this is the field the shared bundled fragments (e.g. `test-paths`/`test-paths-stories`) are typically used for.

attr_present.description: Attribute gate: keep a finding only when this file carries a truthy attribute of this name, injected via an overlay's per-file `attributes` (an exact `{"file":{"path":...}}` target wins, else the longest covering `{"pathScope":{"prefix":...}}`). A plain attribute name, NOT a regex, and NOT fragment-expanded. Lets a rule consume a project's own declaration instead of inferring it from names or shapes. Evaluated as a whole-tree post-filter after the per-file pass (attributes are not a cache-key ingredient), so it can only REMOVE findings and only per file.

attr_absent.description: Same lookup as `attr_present`, inverted: keep a finding only when the file carries NO truthy value for the attribute. On its own this gate is inert when nobody declares the name (every file trivially lacks it, so the rule fires everywhere) — pair it with `require_attr_declared` when the attribute is one a USER declares rather than one the engine mints.

require_attr_declared.description: Precondition on the declaration channel itself: the rule runs only when at least one attribute with this name exists anywhere in the analysis (target shape and truthiness irrelevant — an explicit `false` still counts as an answer). With nothing declared the rule emits nothing, and the run's `warnings` disclose that it did not run, which name it needed, how many candidate sites went unjudged, and how to declare one. For a rule whose premise is a project-specific fact the source cannot state.

snippet_max.description: Max snippet length in the finding (long lines truncate).

type.description: Multi-pattern co-occurrence within one symbol's body span (e.g. exec + string concatenation in the SAME method). Needs parser-projected symbol spans; files without them are silently skipped.

file_pattern.description: Target file-path regex — the rule only scans matching files.

require_file.description: Cheap pre-skip: only scan a file whose whole text matches this regex. Absent = always scan. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

require_file_all.description: Additional pre-skip regexes, ALL of which must match the file text.

require_file_absent.description: Negated pre-skip: if ANY of these matches the whole file text, the rule skips the file entirely.

skip_comment_lines.description: Skip lines whose trimmed start opens a comment in THAT FILE's own syntax — `//`, `*`, `/*` for every extension, plus `--` in a `.sql` file (one extension-keyed leader table, not a fixed triple).

strip_string_literals.description: Mask closed string-literal interiors on each line to spaces before testing any `patterns`/`absent` regex, so a token inside a string literal does not false-fire. The original line still supplies the snippet + marker context. Leave false for rules whose intent is to match INSIDE strings.

patterns.description: ALL of these must match somewhere within one symbol's body span for a finding.

trigger.description: The `patterns[].label` whose first (top-down) match supplies the finding's line and snippet.

trigger_in_loop.description: Structural gate: a trigger match only counts when it falls inside one of the file's projected loop spans (loop statement or array-iteration callback body). Files with no loop spans can never satisfy the trigger (graceful degrade).

require_call_kind.description: Structural gate — a call KIND (a plain string compared for equality, NOT a regex). The scanned symbol span must contain at least one projected call site of that kind, i.e. the parser witnessed a real use of the API family inside this method body. It replaces the CO-OCCURRENCE half a rule would otherwise spell as a bare-token `patterns` arm (a local variable named `exec` satisfies a regex; a projected site cannot be one), while `patterns`/`trigger`/`absent` stay lexical — only the witness becomes structural. Degrades to SILENCE like `trigger_in_loop` and for the same reason (the gate ALLOWS on evidence): no projected sites, or a callee the producer cannot resolve, means no finding, so a rule setting this must disclose the trade in its own message. Kind spellings: the authoritative list is `zzop_core::RULE_READ_CALL_KINDS` (see callScan.kind — this description defers rather than enumerates, for the same staleness reason).

after.description: Lexical-ORDER gate on the trigger pattern: names another `patterns[].label` that must already have matched BEFORE a trigger match counts (for both satisfaction and the finding's line). "Before" = an earlier line in the same span, or — on the SAME line — the ordering pattern's first match starting before the trigger pattern's first match. SAME-LINE NESTING RESIDUAL: that offset comparison cannot tell a callee that FOLLOWS the trigger from one nested INSIDE its arguments, which evaluates first — `await redis.set(k, Number(await redis.get(k)) + 1)` and `setData(await fetch(url))` are both silently dropped. Structural, not fixable here; every rule whose trigger can span a nested call discloses it in its own message. Setting it also fixes the anchor: the finding lands on the first trigger match that actually follows, not on the first one anywhere in the span. Proves lexical order in the SOURCE TEXT, not execution order (a trigger in an `else` branch, or in a callback declared after the ordering token but invoked before it, still counts) — strictly stronger than co-occurrence, strictly weaker than dataflow, so a rule using it should say "lexically after" in its message. Naming a label no `patterns` entry declares is malformed and skips the rule, exactly like `trigger`. Absent = no ordering requirement (plain co-occurrence). NOT a regex — a label name, never fragment-expanded or regex-checked.

after_in_same_function.description: Structural PAIRING gate on `after` — a no-op without it: the ordering label's match must fall INSIDE the innermost projected `function_spans` entry containing the trigger, not merely inside the same symbol body span. Exists because a method-scan span is a DECLARED symbol's body — a React component's whole function — so `after` otherwise pairs a setter in one closure with an `await` in an unrelated SIBLING closure. CONTAINMENT, not span identity: an enclosing function's own boundary stays visible to a trigger in that same function even when the boundary's line is also covered by a nested merged continuation span. A file with no projected function spans degrades to a NO-OP (every line resolves to "no enclosing function", so all lines count as the same one), leaving the rule's pre-gate behavior intact — the opposite direction from `trigger_in_loop`'s silence, and deliberate: this gate only ever REMOVES pairings, so "remove nothing" preserves coverage instead of deleting it. That degrade is decided PER LINE, not per file: a trigger line inside no projected span reads as "no gate on this line", never as "no pair" — a missing span is absence of evidence, so it re-admits the pre-gate scope rather than deleting a finding on a fact nobody has. Reachable with spans PRESENT: a class body's own top level (a class's body span is the scanned unit when the class declares no method/constructor, and a property-initializer line there is inside no function span), or an external parser that projects `function_spans` only partially.

absent.description: Vetoes: after every `patterns` entry is satisfied, the finding is dropped if ANY of these also matches a line in the SAME span (e.g. a guarding try/catch or `$transaction(...)` wrapper).

file_exclude_pattern.description: Path regex — a file whose relative path matches is skipped entirely. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

snippet_max.description: Max snippet length in the finding (long lines truncate).

type.description: Query over a file's projected symbol declarations (naming-convention / banned-export style rules). Filters AND together. Runs in envelope mode too.

file_pattern.description: Target file-path regex — narrows the file set before symbol filters apply.

kind.description: Restrict to one symbol kind (zzop_core::SourceSymbolKind, lowercase serde form). Absent = any kind.

name_pattern.description: Regex on the symbol name — fires on a match, or on a NON-match under `negate: true`. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

exported.description: Restrict to exported (`true`) or non-exported (`false`) symbols. Absent = both.

negate.description: Flips `name_pattern` from "must match" to "must not match" (e.g. "every exported component must be PascalCase"). With no `name_pattern`, every symbol passes.

type.description: Query over a file's projected IoFacts (boundary-convention rules, e.g. "every HTTP endpoint must be versioned"). Filters AND together. Runs in envelope mode too.

file_pattern.description: Target file-path regex — narrows the file set before io filters apply.

direction.description: Which side(s) of the file's IoFacts to query (zzop_core::IoDirection, lowercase serde form).

kind.description: Exact match against the io entry's kind string (open vocabulary — e.g. "http", "db-table", "env", "topic"). Absent = any kind.

key_pattern.description: Regex on the entry's normalized key — fires on a match, or on a NON-match under `negate: true`. An entry with an unresolved (null) key never matches; under `negate: true` that makes it a hit. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

negate.description: Flips `key_pattern` from "must match" to "must not match".

file_exclude_pattern.description: Path regex evaluated right after `file_pattern` (cheapest gate first) — an entry whose file matches is skipped entirely. Same shape as line-scan's field of the same name. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

symbol_pattern.description: Regex on a provide's `symbol` — PROVIDES-ONLY evidence: a consume never carries a symbol, and a provide whose symbol is absent never matches (never-guess). `negate` does NOT flip this field; it is a plain must-match gate applied after `negate` has resolved `key_pattern`.

attr_absent.description: Matches only when the tree's AttributeStore has NO truthy value for this attribute on the entry's route (exact IoKey wins, else the longest covering PathScope). An entry with no resolved key always satisfies this gate. A plain attribute name, NOT a regex.

attr_present.description: Matches only when that same attribute lookup IS truthy. An entry with no resolved key never satisfies this gate. A plain attribute name, NOT a regex.

anchor_exclude_pattern.description: Regex applied to the anchor line's own source text (the provide/consume's own line). When no source text is reachable (envelope mode with no native source) the exclusion simply does not apply — never a guessed match.

type.description: Query over a file's projected CALL SITES (zzop_core::call_sites::CallSite — `kind` + `line` + the callee exactly as written). Unlike a line-scan over the same idea, a site comes from a parse, so a mention inside a string literal or a comment is not one, and `in_loop` can cross it with the file's loop spans. COVERAGE, stated plainly: the TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Java and C# parsers ship call-site producers for both families (`console-write` + `env-read`); the Rust parser ships the `env-read` family ONLY (it deliberately emits no console-write — no shipped rule admits `.rs` for that family); Prisma and SQL have no producer arm, so this channel is empty there and a call-scan rule admitting one of them fires nowhere on it. Its absent-fact degrade is SILENCE, never a claim that a file is clean.

file_pattern.description: Target file-path regex — narrows the file set before any site filter applies. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

file_exclude_pattern.description: Path regex evaluated right after `file_pattern` (cheapest gate first) — a file whose relative path matches is skipped entirely. Same shape as line-scan's field of the same name. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

kind.description: Exact match against a site's kind string (open vocabulary — the authoritative list of spellings this build's rules read is `zzop_core::RULE_READ_CALL_KINDS`, pinned by rule_contracts::call_kind_readers; a closed enumeration here went stale twice in one day, so this description deliberately defers instead of listing). Absent = any family. A kind no producer emits is not an error and not a warning at load time; it is silence. The vocabulary is open by design, so the pack loader cannot tell a typo from a family some adapter fills — what records which kinds this build's rules actually read is `zzop_core::RULE_READ_CALL_KINDS`.

callee_pattern.description: Regex on the callee EXACTLY as the source wrote it (`console.error`, `os.environ.get`). This is where a rule's semantic judgment goes: the channel deliberately carries no level/stream/severity field, because JavaScript's `error` is a member-name tag, Python's `file=sys.stderr` is an argument, and only Rust's `log::error!` names a real severity — folding the three into one field would assert an equivalence the source never made. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

algorithm_pattern.description: Regex on the site's `algorithm` — the one argument-derived fact this channel carries (today the `hash-call` family only). EVIDENCE-ALLOWING and never-guess on both sides: a site whose algorithm is absent (the source did not spell one, e.g. `createHash(algoVar)` / `hashlib.new(name)`, or the family carries none) NEVER matches when this field is set, so a rule filtering on it goes silent rather than approximating. Matched against the spelling exactly as written (`md5`, `MD5`, `SHA-1`), so a rule's pattern owns its own case-insensitivity — the same original-spelling contract `callee_pattern` is under. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

line_pattern.description: LEXICAL residual on the site's own source line: a regex the line text must ALSO match for the site to count. This is how a call-scan rule keeps a co-occurrence half that is genuinely textual (`security/weak-password-hash` requires a credential word on the hashing line) while its trigger stays structural — the inverse of line-scan's `line_call_kind`, which adds a structural gate to a lexical rule. Degrades to SILENCE one step further than the sibling gates: a site whose line the file text cannot supply (envelope mode carries no source lines) has nothing to match and does not fire, which deliberately inverts the channel's "anchor text is a courtesy" rule for the rules that opt in — a rule whose CLAIM includes "on the same line as X" cannot honestly fire without the line. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

in_loop.description: Structural gate: the site only counts when its line falls inside one of the file's projected loop spans, i.e. the parser PROVED the call runs once per iteration. Reads the same `loop_spans` fact `method-scan`'s `trigger_in_loop` does, with the same degrade: a file with no loop spans can never satisfy it (silence, never a permissive fallback).

attr_present.description: Attribute gate, identical in contract to line-scan's field of the same name: keep a finding only when this file carries a truthy attribute of this name (exact `{"file":{"path":...}}` target wins, else the longest covering `{"pathScope":{"prefix":...}}`). A plain attribute name, NOT a regex, and NOT fragment-expanded. Evaluated as a whole-tree post-filter after the per-file pass, so it can only REMOVE findings and only per file.

attr_absent.description: Same lookup as `attr_present`, inverted. Inert when nobody declares the name (every file trivially lacks it, so the rule fires everywhere) — pair it with `require_attr_declared` when the attribute is one a USER declares rather than one the engine mints.

require_attr_declared.description: Precondition on the declaration channel itself: the rule runs only when at least one attribute with this name exists anywhere in the analysis. With nothing declared the rule emits nothing and the run's `warnings` disclose that it did not run, which name it needed, how many candidate sites went unjudged, and how to declare one.

snippet_max.description: Max snippet length in the finding — the site's own source line, trimmed. A site whose line the file text cannot supply (envelope mode carries no source lines) still produces a finding, with an empty snippet: the site is the evidence, the line text only a courtesy.

type.description: Query over a file's projected BOUND STRING LITERALS (zzop_core::BoundStringLiteral — binding name + value hash + extraction-time Shannon entropy, NEVER the value text). The two judgments a line-scan regex structurally cannot make: name↔value comparison (needs a cross-group backreference regex does not have) and an entropy floor (not computable from a match at all). Because the value is hashed at extraction, no candidate secret is ever stored in the cache — and no VALUE-text veto is expressible (mock-/test- prefixes on the value); name-side vetoes are (`name_exclude_pattern`). Filters AND together, evaluated cheap-first in the order listed below. A finding on this channel carries NO source-line snippet, deliberately: the literal's line IS the candidate secret. Absent-fact degrade is SILENCE: a file with no projected literals (no producer for its language, a degraded parse, an oversized file, envelope mode) matches nothing — under-report, never a clean claim.

file_pattern.description: Target file-path regex (e.g. `(?i)\.(ts|tsx|js|java|rs|py|go|cs)$`) — narrows the file set before any literal filter applies. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

file_exclude_pattern.description: Path regex evaluated right after `file_pattern` (cheapest gate first) — a file whose relative path matches is skipped entirely. Same shape as line-scan's field of the same name. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

name_pattern.description: Regex on the entry's BINDING NAME, matched against the spelling exactly as written (`apiKey`, `CLIENT_SECRET`). Absent = every named literal in the selected files. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

name_exclude_pattern.description: Negated regex on the binding NAME — an entry whose name matches is skipped. The mock/test/placeholder veto lives HERE on this channel: a value-side veto is impossible by design (the value is hashed at extraction — see `type`), so a rule that wants both keeps name-side hygiene here and accepts the published value-side loss. ${NAME} fragment reference supported.

entropy_min.description: Entropy floor in TOTAL Shannon bits (zzop_core::shannon_entropy_bits is the exact formula the producers bake in): the entry only matches when its extraction-time entropy >= entropy_min. Absent = no floor. A threshold is a POLICY VALUE and belongs in the pack, never hardcoded in the engine.

skip_value_equals_name.description: Veto the sentinel shape `refresh_token = "refresh_token"`: skip an entry whose value is LITERALLY its own binding name, compared by hash — exact equality only, which is all a hash can honestly answer (no case-folding, no separator-normalizing; the line-scan twin's broader shape vetoes do not transfer).
